newsitem.title: USA: US Airways sees union allegations as "unfounded".
newsitem.headline: US Airways sees union allegations as "unfounded".

text.p: US Airways Group Inc said Thursday a lawsuit filed by its pilots makes "unfounded and frivolous" allegations which divert attention from reaching a contract pact that would make the airline more competitive, allow it to grow and give its employees job security.

"We have offered our pilots a contractual guarantee that will give them compensation parity with our major competitors -- American, Delta, Northwest and United -- and we have guaranteed that we will expand the airline at a rate comparable to these major competitors," US Airways said in a written statement.
"We should be focusing our time and attention on concluding an agreement, rather than on a divisive and frivolous lawsuit," the company said.

Earlier on Thursday, the pilots union filed a lawsuit in federal district court in Pittsburgh, alleging that US Airways' recent actions and statements "are intended to subvert and impair" contract negotiations.
US Airways, the nation's sixth largest airline, has been in labor talks with its pilots since their contract became amendable in April 1996.

The lawsuit, which was filed in federal district court in Pittsburgh, seeks injunctive relief against "further improper conduct," as well as damages under the Railway Labor Act, the federal statute that governs the airline industry's labor relations.

US Airways has laid off pilots and threatened additional layoffs, base closings, downsizing and cancellation of aircraft orders if the pilots do not comply with management's position for a new contract, the union said in its lawsuit.
US Airways' actions are intended "to unduly influence the outcome of negotiations," the union said.
